title: Lease vs licence - a distinction that changes everything legally
p1:
Two people can occupy the same property, pay money every month, and still have completely different legal rights.

The difference often comes down to one word: lease or licence.
p2:
Many assume that if someone is allowed to use a property for a period of time, they automatically have a lease. That is not always true.

A lease usually gives a person a legal interest in the property, while a licence only gives permission to use it. A licence generally does not create the same level of protection or control.
p3:
The surprising part? Calling an agreement a 'licence' does not decide its legal nature. Courts often look at the actual arrangement, such as whether the person has exclusive possession and control of the space.

This distinction can affect eviction rights, responsibilities, and long-term security. Before signing any property agreement, the label matters less than the real terms behind it.
conclusion: Have you ever signed a rental or property agreement without knowing whether it was a lease or just a licence? What was your experience?
